title: Beat the Reference
lesson: A human-designed layout can make a different trade-off from an automated one.
brief: This Clifford circuit has one especially noisy CNOT. Checkpoint includes a reference layout generated by qiskit-paulice using the same check budget. Try to meet or beat the reference on both Fidelity and Yield.
learning_moment: The reference is produced by qiskit-paulice, which chooses checks using its own optimization objective. Checkpoint scores both layouts using this game's Fidelity and Yield metrics. Because the objectives are not identical, a hand-designed layout can sometimes do better under this game's scoring rule. Treat this as a comparison between two objectives on this circuit, not proof that a person always outperforms an automated method.
hint: Start with the highlighted weak CNOT. Use one check to target the errors around it, then decide whether a second check should cover a wider or shorter span. Compare both Fidelity and Yield with the reference.
reflection: Which metric made your layout better or worse than the automated reference?
noise_note: One two-qubit gate is much noisier than the others; look for its highlighted error-rate badge.

noise.label: level noise with one weak CNOT (q1-q2)

explanation: The weak CNOT is between q1 and q2 (the orange badge).
Check B starts on two qubits just before it: X on q0 and Z on q2. The weak CNOT copies the Z onto q1, so check B watches both of its qubits.
Check A, X on q3 from slot 2, stays X until the final H turns it into Z. It watches the last CNOT between q2 and q3. Both checks end at the readout.
Together they beat the reference on both Fidelity and Yield. The reference optimises its own measure of undetected errors, not this game's score.
